questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The fact that UC Irvine has the second-highest rated Department of Criminology in the United States and I want to pursue a PhD in criminology. The weather in California was also important.

questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy through Blackrock's ACC. It's an evil company though, and you have very little rights as a tenant.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That transiting from VDC to UCI campus or the supermarkets/restaurants in the weekend is a hassle without a car and without the busses running.

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Very confusing and very chaotic. I ended up participating in all the impacted classes that I wanted to, however, but it took a lot of effort and direct emailing of professors.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Some professors were helpful, others were not. Other times, administrative employees were helpful in providing enrolment codes for specific courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: There was one class I did not manage to enrol in, but other than that, I was very successful despite the criminology courses being impacted and highly popular.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Plan out way ahead of time which courses you are interested in. Read up on UCI's reddit page how to enrol in impacted courses. Message administrative employees regarding how to enrol in impacted courses. Message professors politely and display your interest in their course to be admitted ahead of other students.

Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level in the US is a joke and is akin to high school in Denmark. Some courses, e.g., professor Novaco's "Violence in Society" was quite challenging, however. Sociology classes at UCPH are MUCH more challenging and rigorous. I will say, however, that the structure of the courses at UCI is very easy to understand. I have experienced more often than not that the complexity of the courses at UCPH's Sociology department makes it difficult for professors to convey the intentions and learning goals of their courses, making the courses unnecessarily difficult.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much more memorization instead of critical thinking and practical application. At UCI, it is a lot of multiple choice tests, and the critical engagement is limited to reflection papers without data collection or actual research practice.

questions.answer:
The Social Animal
Violence in Society

The lecturers were much more skilled in these courses, and the courses were much more challenging. It seemed like the lecturers cared about our learning here, and that the lecturers enjoyed teaching.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
The insurance was higher than expected since you pay it individually for both quarters I attended.

Southern California is made for cars, and if you don't have a car or friends with cars, you will be spending exorbitant amounts of money on Uber. The public transport system is a literal joke. I cannot stress this enough that you should either buy a car in the beginning of your exchange to sell it once you leave, or set aside a significant portion of money for Uber. Also try to ride Ubers together in groups, since it is a lot cheaper.

When renting at ACC, the lease period is 12 months, and I was only there for 6 months. The rent is paid 2 months in advance, meaning I had to pay 2 additional installments of rent for months I wasn't going to live there. This money is returned to me in USD in a physical letter to Denmark, which is absolutely ridiculous. This is back to ACC being owned by Blackrock - a thoroughly terrible corporation - and the fact that the US in some regards is not as digitalized as Denmark.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Groceries were extraordinarily expensive, since rent costs in Irvine are artificially high, being owned by the private Irvine Company, and since many college students cannot get away from Irvine to shop. 

Tipping is a huge expense if you don't want your waiters hating on you. You can avoid tipping if you're never coming back to the restaurant/business, but if you plan on coming back, leaving a tip is smart.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Much more than in Denmark. Most clubs were ethnically segregated though, which seemed kind of racist. Asians with Asians, Whites with Whites, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hiking club, binge drinking in Newport and LA, going to the ARC Gym

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: San Francisco, Yosemite, Grand Canyon, Tijuana, Los Angeles, Las Vegas.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy. All my roommates were Mexican Americans and they were cool.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None, really. One annoying thing is that Americans in the service industry tend to ask "How are you?" instead of just saying "Hi" which is kind of annoying, as it prompts a conversation you don't necessarily want. Probably another great reason to abolish tipping culture.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Outgoing-ness of Americans is great.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't be worried about making friends and finding people you connect with. It is inevitable.

Watch out for stingy people. Identify them early on and steer clear of them, as lack of generosity is a huge red flag. I suppose stinginess is more prevalent on exchange, since everyone will be leaving soon anyways and don't need to keep up appearances and maintain social ties.

Remember to focus on academics. Even though the difficulty of the courses is a joke, you can still learn a lot more by putting in effort.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't miss the deadlines of ACC registration and payment. It is much earlier than you think.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Transportation.

questions.answer: Yes
